summary: This binary is GNU Octave 4.2.1 octave-config, a legitimate configuration utility built with MinGW/GCC via the MXE cross-compile system. It prints Octave installation paths and configuration values (BINDIR, DATADIR, LIBDIR, VERSION, etc.) when invoked with -p <key>. No packing, obfuscation, anti-analysis, or malware indicators were found. The binary is a clean standard C++ console application with 150 functions, all statically linked CRT and libstdc++ routines, no network imports, no crypto imports, and no suspicious strings.

findings.title: Binary identified as GNU Octave octave-config utility
findings.description: The binary is GNU Octave 4.2.1 octave-config.exe, a command-line tool that prints Octave installation configuration paths. Built with MinGW/GCC via the MXE cross-compile system.
findings.reasoning: The binary contains 30+ Octave path strings referencing /scratch/jwe/mxe-octave/4.2.1/w64-32/usr/x86_64-w64-mingw32, environment variable names like OCTAVE_HOME, VERSION=4.2.1, usage text for octave-config CLI, and the main function implements a config-key query parser with -p, -v, --help options.

evidence.observation: Usage text: "octave-config: unrecognized argument", "usage: octave-config [options]", -v, --version, --m-site-dir, --oct-site-dir help text
main() implements argument parsing for -p, -h, -v, --m-site-dir, --oct-site-dir, queries std::map config and prints to stdout/cerr
sub_401AD0 populates ~30 config keys (OCTAVE_HOME, PREFIX, BINDIR, DATADIR, VERSION=4.2.1, etc.) into std::map
OCTAVE_HOME resolver reads env var or derives from GetModuleFileNameA, strips \bin\ suffix

limitations: Dynamic confirmation would verify OCTAVE_HOME resolution and output format

findings.title: No packing or obfuscation detected
findings.description: The binary is a standard MinGW-compiled executable with no packing, encryption, compression, or obfuscation of code or data sections.
findings.reasoning: Standard section layout (.text, .data, .rdata, .pdata, .xdata, .bss, .idata, .edata, .CRT, .tls, .reloc) with normal sizes and characteristics. .text section has low byte diversity. No section entropy anomalies. All 150 functions are recognized by IDA Pro with standard MinGW CRT/C++ signatures. No decode/decrypt loops, no suspicious GetProcAddress patterns, no runtime unpacking stubs.

sources.location: IDA Pro survey_binary, PE header analysis, function analysis

evidence.observation: 11 standard sections with normal sizes and characteristics. No packed-section anomalies.
150 functions recognized, 99 named, 1 library function, 50 unnamed (all standard MinGW CRT helpers)

source.location: IDA Pro decompile analysis of all functions

evidence.observation: No XOR loops, decryption routines, base64 decoding, or compression stubs found in any function

findings.title: No anti-analysis mechanisms detected
findings.description: The binary contains no anti-debugging, anti-VM, sandbox evasion, or integrity-checking mechanisms.
findings.reasoning: No anti-debug import (IsDebuggerPresent, NtQueryInformationProcess, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, PEB walking). No anti-VM strings or hardware detection. GetTickCount and QueryPerformanceCounter are used only for random seed generation. SetUnhandledExceptionFilter is standard MinGW crash reporting, not obfuscated control flow. No integrity checks, timing checks, or exception-driven obfuscation.

sources.location: IDA Pro imports analysis, function decompile

evidence.observation: Imports only KERNEL32 (basic process/thread/time/critical section), msvcrt, libstdc++-6, libgcc_s_seh-1. No anti-debug APIs.
GetTickCount and QueryPerformanceCounter used exclusively for seed generation, XORed with time/PID/TID

findings.title: Standard MinGW CRT execution path
findings.description: The binary follows the standard MinGW CRT entry path: start -> CRT init -> main() -> octave-config logic -> exit. No alternative entry points, no early injection, no unusual startup sequences.
findings.reasoning: Entry point at 0x1500 (RVA) maps to start @ 0x401500. The CRT startup initializes the SEH filter, C++ runtime, pseudo-relocations, exception table, and FPU, then calls main(). The main() function at 0x404ec0 is a straightforward octave-config CLI parser. TLS callbacks manage standard MinGW TLS cleanup.

evidence.observation: start() calls sub_403040 (seed) then sub_4011B0 (CRT startup)
CRT startup: initterm, SEH filter, pseudo-reloc, SEH tables, FPU init, then calls main()
TlsCallback_0 (0x403250) and TlsCallback_1 (0x403220) call sub_403F30 for standard TLS cleanup

findings.title: No network capabilities detected
findings.description: The binary has zero network imports (no Winsock, WinHTTP, WinINet, or URL-related functions). No network-related strings found.
findings.reasoning: Import analysis shows only KERNEL32, msvcrt, libstdc++-6, and libgcc_s_seh-1. No ws2_32, winhttp, wininet, urlmon, or any socket-related DLL. No URLs, IP addresses, or domain names in strings.

evidence.observation: No network DLLs imported. Only KERNEL32, msvcrt, libstdc++-6, libgcc_s_seh-1.
No URLs, IP addresses, or domain names in the binary string table

findings.title: Embedded Octave compile-time configuration
findings.description: The binary embeds a compile-time configuration database of ~30 Octave install paths and the OCTAVE_HOME resolution logic. This is the expected configuration data for octave-config and is not suspicious.
findings.reasoning: sub_401AD0 populates a std::map<string,string> with hardcoded paths from the MXE build environment. The OCTAVE_HOME resolver at sub_401530 reads the environment variable or derives the install prefix from the executable path. All paths are consistent with Octave 4.2.1 for x86_64-w64-mingw32.

evidence.observation: ~30 config keys populated into std::map: OCTAVE_HOME, PREFIX, BINDIR, DATADIR, LIBDIR, VERSION=4.2.1, etc.
OCTAVE_HOME resolver: reads env var, if not set uses GetModuleFileNameA and strips \bin\ suffix

findings.title: No persistence mechanisms detected
findings.description: The binary contains no registry, filesystem, or service persistence mechanisms.
findings.reasoning: No registry API imports (RegOpenKeyEx, RegSetValueEx, etc.). No service manager imports. No scheduled task, startup folder, or run key strings. No file write operations beyond fwrite from C runtime.

evidence.observation: No registry API imports, no service manager imports, no persistence-related function calls

findings.title: No process injection capabilities detected
findings.description: The binary contains no process injection, API hooking, or code injection capabilities.
findings.reasoning: No VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread, SetWindowsHookEx, or any process manipulation APIs. The VirtualProtect import is used by the standard MinGW pseudo-relocation handler for DLL base relocation fixups.

evidence.observation: No injection-related APIs. VirtualProtect is used by pseudo-reloc handler (standard MinGW).
